slides.title: The comma splice: the SAT's favorite ^^wrong answer^^
Joining two full sentences
slides.body: A comma alone can **never** join two complete sentences. If both sides could stand alone, the comma-only choice is wrong. Eliminate it instantly.

slides.title: The semicolon test
slides.body: A semicolon works anywhere a period works. So if two answer choices differ only by period vs. semicolon, they are *both* wrong — the test cannot have two right answers.

slides.title: The splice in the wild
slides.body: "The tide was rising, the crew hurried to shore." Both halves are complete sentences, so a comma cannot join them. Fix: period, semicolon, or comma + *and/but/so*.
slides.tip: Both sides stand alone? The comma can't hold them.
